thread:
olivia (support): getting a spike of customer complaints about p95/p99 on embeddings & chat endpoints from eu-west-1 since ~03:05 UTC. multiple customers report timeouts and elevated tail latencies
anya (oncall): seen alert too — apm shows p99 for /v1/embeddings up from 180ms -> 1.6s, error rate slight uptick 0.3% -> 1.2%
sam (eng-runtime): any infra changes rolled in that window? models, drivers, or rollout?
marcus (eng-infra): we did a staged CUDA15 driver push to eu-west auto-roll group at 02:40 UTC, ~40 nodes in pool A. rollout hit ~60% by 03:00 then continued.
olivia (support): customers say regressions coincide with that. sending repro steps from cust: short series of embedding requests with concurrency 8 reproduces tail on their side.
sam (eng-runtime): looking at traces — KV-cache miss rate jumped at same time. kernel I/O p99 on nvme also spiked on several nodes. suspect host-side storage noise leading to GPU stalls.
marcus (eng-infra): grabbing host metrics now. snippet from node eu-w1-node-27 syslog around 03:02:
```
[03:02:11] nvme0: queue-depth 1024 -> qlen spike
[03:02:13] nvme_io: rq completion latency 120ms -> 900ms
[03:02:17] nvidia: gpu stall detected, pagefault retry
```
anya (oncall): deploy-bot shows driver rollout batch 4 completed 03:01 on that node. correlation looks strong.
sam (eng-runtime): chain hypothesis: CUDA15 driver changes + small udev/firmware interaction caused intermittent NVMe IO latency -> model weight page-ins / KV-cache fills have higher host IO -> GPU scheduler stalls -> token emission tail. also retries from clients amplify load.
marcus (eng-infra): immediate mitigations: 1) pause/rollback driver rollout to batch 3 (nodes not yet upgraded), 2) cordon/evict the worst nodes, 3) route traffic away from eu-west degraded pool to eu-central fallback for premium customers. executing now.
deploy-bot: rollback command issued: `imgctl node rollback --group eu-west-auto --target-batch 3 --reason "nvme tail latency after cuda15"`
anya (oncall): cordoned eu-w1-node-27/31/42 and drained pods: `kubectl cordon eu-w1-node-27 && kubectl drain eu-w1-node-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
sam (eng-runtime): enabling fallback to quantized smaller model for low-latency tiers to reduce KV cache pressure: `route: embeddings -> model-embed-v2-q8` for route ids matching tier:low-latency. Doing a short canary for 10% traffic.
olivia (support): notified affected customers about mitigation and temporary routing; they asked about billing impact — any ETA for full rollback or fix?
marcus (eng-infra): after drain/rollback p99 on affected nodes dropped from 1.6s -> ~230ms within 4 minutes for routed traffic. we'll keep nodes out of rotation until driver issue triaged + nvme firmware probe. target to finish rollback and full validation in next 2 hours.
sam (eng-runtime): next steps for root cause: 1) bisect which CUDA15 component triggers increased NVMe latency (probe small kernel/firmware combos), 2) run local repro with kernel tracing (blk_trace + ibtb), 3) reproduce KV-cache page-in path to confirm pagefault pattern. I'll own runtime traces and add histogram exports.
anya (oncall): opening incident ticket and postmortem stub. tagging oncall rotation and infra owners.
sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-3453 by anya — severity: high — customers impacted: multiple eu embeddings customers.
olivia (support): thanks team. I'll update customers with rollback + timeline and mention fallback routing to reduce tail. will escalate billing concerns if customers ask for credits.
marcus (eng-infra): collecting dmesg + nvme SMART from cordoned nodes, will upload to the incident doc and link after gather. also will run driver rollback validation script: `./verify-driver-p95.sh eu-west-auto`
sam (eng-runtime): adding a short-term mitigation: reduce auth token refresh rate for internal LB to avoid client-side retry storms while we stabilize. note: this may increase token TTL memory but reduces retry amplification.
anya (oncall): monitoring dashboards show p99 trending back down for eu-west overall but we'll keep reduced traffic policies until full verification.
sam (eng-runtime): will post final triage and recommended next steps in the incident doc: revert rollout, NVMe vendor engagement if needed, and a smaller kernel/driver compatibility matrix for future rollouts.
olivia (support): closing loop with the customers now. thanks all :thumbsup:
